title: TestMu AI and RiskMandate

scenes.kicker: RiskMandate · a story made at the summit
scenes.title: TestMu AI and RiskMandate
scenes.caption: For TestMu AI

scenes.title: TestMu AI grades what an agent actually did
items: Agent Assurance tests agents that act: tool calls, file writes, API calls
Rook CLI finds the agent, writes functional and adversarial scenarios, runs them live
Each criterion graded from evidence: Pass, Fail, Unable to Verify
Unable to Verify is counted separately, not hidden in a pass
The agent's own reply is the weakest signal
scenes.caption: From their own public pages: a verdict built on recorded effects, not on what the agent says.
say: TestMu AI, formerly LambdaTest, grades agents on what they changed, not on what they say they did.
Recorded tool calls, command output, exit status and changed files carry the verdict.
scenes.source: TestMu AI public pages (Agent Assurance, Rook CLI)

scenes.text: "Rook does not sandbox or roll back the agent under test. Refunds, emails, tickets, database updates, and filesystem writes happen in the target environment."
scenes.caption: Quoted from TestMu AI's Rook documentation. The actions are real. This is where a mandate and a harness fit.
say: This is their own sentence, and it is honest: the test run has real effects.
Proof arrives after the action. Something has to define and enforce what the agent may do before it acts. That is the harness.

scenes.title: Policy, then enforcement, then proof
steps: Policy: RiskMandate sets what the agent may do
Enforcement: our harness holds the agent to it
Proof: Rook grades what the agent actually did
scenes.caption: What we would do together: our hypothesis, built from public pages only.
say: Three steps, each owned by the right party: we set and enforce the limits, they prove what happened.
Nothing of theirs was tested; this is a hypothesis.

scenes.title: Two halves of one record
rows: Observed effects: tool calls, file changes, API calls
Mandate: what the agent may do
What happened in the target environment
What the agent could have reached beyond those effects
scenes.caption: Their gap is between claim and proof; ours is between mandate and reach. Our hypothesis, not their claim.
say: Unable to Verify marks where proof runs out.
Reach marks where the mandate and the agent's actual access part ways. Together they make one record.

scenes.title: A pilot: one of our agents, two reports

before.label: Rook run
items: Rook CLI run against one of our agents
Pass, Fail and Unable to Verify counted separately

after.label: ABP run report
items: The same agent's ABP run report
What the mandate allowed and what the harness enforced

scenes.caption: What we would do together: no results yet; the pilot is how we would find out.
say: One agent of ours, run through Rook, with its ABP run report beside it.
We read the two side by side to see what each one shows that the other does not.

scenes.title: Two ways the pieces connect
items: Our ABP policies become Rook criteria: what the agent may do, graded from evidence
Rook's verdicts become evidence in mandate reports
Claim, proof, mandate and reach in one record
scenes.caption: Our hypothesis, not their claim: policy flows into their grading, their verdicts flow back into our reports.
say: Rook already writes criteria for an agent; an ABP policy states what the agent may do, so the policy can be the criteria.
Their verdicts then give our reports the proof of what really happened.

scenes.text: Rook proves what the agent did. A mandate and a harness decide what it may do. Together: policy, then enforcement, then proof.
scenes.caption: Our suggestion, built from public pages only.
say: Because the actions are real, the limit has to come before the grade.

scenes.text: A pilot: Rook run against one of our agents, beside its ABP run report.
scenes.caption: agent@riskmandate.ai
say: Start small: one agent, one Rook run, one mandate report, side by side.
